title: Francis and the wolf
hookLine: Francis makes peace between the town of Gubbio and a hungry wolf (Little Flowers of St Francis 21)

cards: Every town has a wolf. Maybe not a real one: the neighbor everyone avoids, the kid at school who bites back, the relative who ruins every holiday dinner.
The usual answer is walls, avoidance, maybe a group chat to complain in.
In the old story, the Italian hill town of Gubbio had a real wolf, big and hungry, and the townspeople had stopped leaving the walls without weapons.
Then Francis of Assisi walked out of the gate toward it, though they told him not to.

teach.b: Francis is remembered as a merchant's son who gave away everything. In his Canticle of the Creatures he calls the sun his brother and the moon his sister, and the stories say he preached to birds.

This one comes from the Little Flowers of Saint Francis, a collection of tales about him and his companions, written down after his time: a story told about him, the way families tell stories about a grandparent.
A fierce wolf is killing animals, and even people, around Gubbio. Francis goes out to meet it. The wolf rushes at him with open jaws.

Francis makes the sign of the cross and says, come here, Brother Wolf, and tells it, in Christ's name, not to hurt him or anyone. The wolf closes its mouth and lies down at his feet. Now watch what Francis does.
He doesn't only scold the wolf.
He names what it's done, and then why: it was hungry. So he makes a deal with both sides. The town will feed the wolf every day, and the wolf will harm no one again.
The story says the wolf lifted its paw and put it in Francis's hand as a pledge, right there in the town square, in front of everyone.
For two years after, it went from door to door and was fed, and the dogs didn't even bark at it. When it died of old age, the town grieved.
Brother wolf: not a monster to kill, and not a pet either. A hungry creature, and a town that could afford to feed it. Peace asked something of everyone.

how: Catholics and many other Christians honor Francis of Assisi as a saint of peace and of creation; on or near his feast day, October 4, many churches bless animals.

games.q: you're Francis. the wolf lies quiet at your feet. the town has suffered, and the wolf is starving. what do you do?
o: drive it far away into the mountains
make a pact: the town feeds it, it harms no one

games.why: he makes a pact with both sides: the town feeds the wolf every day, and the wolf pledges, paw in his hand, to harm no one.

practice: Bring to mind a wild creature near where you live, a bird you might set water out for, a squirrel or a crow you could watch without shooing, and picture it clearly. Then think of your wolf, a person who bites.
Without excusing anything, ask what they might be hungry for, and picture offering one small piece of it.

wordCard.voice: Francis. The saint who walked out to meet a killer, saw that it was hungry, and made a peace that fed it. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: brother wolf. Peace began with asking what the wolf was hungry for. Day eighty-nine, done.
